request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The steward's dashboard counts are now over the sheet and all its descendants.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The steward's dashboard now counts over the sheet and all its descendants, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What changed** (front end only; no server or stored-data changes were needed):
- **`features/dashboard/StewardDashboard.tsx`**: the Pending, Review and Overdue counts are now added up over this sheet and every descendant. Each sheet is worked out by its own rules (its own today, rates and settings). Whether the user counts as a steward is still decided by the sheet on screen.
- **`features/counters/ConsolidatedFigures.tsx`**: the app already fetched each descendant's data for its consolidated figures, so the dashboard reuses that. I added an overdue-claim count to each sheet's figures and exported the per-sheet calculation and the descendant-loading hook.

When the screen shows the sheet as of a past date, every sheet in the tree is taken as it stood at the end of that day, the same way the consolidated figures already work.
